edit.statement: 'Is a character in' is functional: a character appears in at most one work.
edit.subject: character_in
edit.original: 'Is a character in' is not functional: a character can appear in several works.
edit.scope: How many distinct works one character can appear in.

direct.prompt: Is the relation 'is a character in' functional, so that a character can appear in only one work?

cross_lingual.prompt: 夏洛克·福尔摩斯是《血字的研究》中的人物，夏洛克·福尔摩斯也是《巴斯克维尔的猎犬》中的人物。能否由此推出《血字的研究》和《巴斯克维尔的猎犬》是同一部作品？

Sherlock Holmes es un personaje de Estudio en escarlata, y Sherlock Holmes también es un personaje de El sabueso de los Baskerville. ¿Se deduce que Estudio en escarlata y El sabueso de los Baskerville son la misma obra?

derived.prompt: Sherlock Holmes is a character in A Study in Scarlet, and Sherlock Holmes is also a character in The Hound of the Baskervilles. Does it follow that A Study in Scarlet and The Hound of the Baskervilles are the same work?
bridge: Sherlock Holmes is a character in A Study in Scarlet, and Sherlock Holmes is also a character in The Hound of the Baskervilles.

derived.prompt: Falstaff is a character in Henry IV, Part 1, and Falstaff is also a character in The Merry Wives of Windsor. Does it follow that Henry IV, Part 1 and The Merry Wives of Windsor are the same work?
bridge: Falstaff is a character in Henry IV, Part 1, and Falstaff is also a character in The Merry Wives of Windsor.

unrelated_near.prompt: Is the relation 'was first published in the year' functional, so that each book has only one year of first publication?

unrelated_far.prompt: Is the relation 'is north of' symmetric?

notes: Locality reference is the logical answer; the scoring gold is the model's own pre-edit answer. Derived premises are hypothetical facts about real works, writers and artists, stated in the prompt. The premises are true, so the new answer (the two works are the same) goes against world knowledge.
